12	/-!
13	# Adelic Riemann–Roch — the residue field of a closed point is the base field
14	
15	This file **discharges** the residue-degree fact `[κ(P) : k̄] = 1` for a prime divisor of
16	an AJC curve over an algebraically closed base field.  It is the input that
17	`Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean` §5–§7 and `Adelic/SectionBounds.lean` §4 both reduce to,
18	and which those files leave open.
19	
20	## What changes relative to `GlobalGeneration.lean` §7
21	
22	`hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed` (there) derives the approximation statement from
23	**three stalk-level instance binders**, and its own docstring records — correctly — that
24	none of them is constructed anywhere in AJC, so that it "trades one unproved fact for
25	three unbuilt instances" and is a *reformulation, not a discharge*.
26	
27	This file builds all three, for a curve `C : Over (Spec k)`, and so closes the gap:
28	
29	1. `Algebra k 𝒪_P` — `stalkStructureHom` (`Picard/TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra.lean`) already
30	   supplies the ring map; what was missing is that it is **compatible with the
31	   `Algebra k K(C)` of `Adelic/GateInstances.lean`**.  That is
32	   `algebraMap_stalk_functionField`, proved by factoring both through `Γ(C,⊤)`:
33	   `stalkStructureHom = constMap ≫ germ_⊤` (`stalkStructureHom_eq_constMap_germ`, from
34	   mathlib's `Hom.germ_stalkMap`), after which mathlib's
35	   `functionField_isScalarTower` matches the two composites.
36	2. `IsScalarTower k 𝒪_P K(C)` — a corollary of (1) (`isScalarTower_stalk_functionField`).
37	3. `Module.Finite k κ_P` — **not needed at all** on this route, which is the substantive
38	   simplification.  §7's argument goes through `IsAlgClosed.algebraMap_bijective_of_isIntegral`,
39	   which needs the residue field to be *integral* over `k` and hence a finiteness input that
40	   AJC does not have.  Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.residueFieldIsoBase` proves
41	   `κ(x) ≅ k` for a closed point of a scheme **locally of finite type** over an
42	   algebraically closed field, obtaining integrality from
43	   `isFinite_iff_locallyOfFiniteType_of_jacobsonSpace` instead.  `LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom`
44	   is a hypothesis a smooth curve satisfies, unlike a bare residue-finiteness gate.
45	
46	So the exchange is: one open fact **out**, and in its place a `LocallyOfFiniteType`
47	hypothesis plus the closedness of the point — both genuinely available.
48	
49	## The N14 finiteness gate falls out too
50	
51	Because the route above needs no finiteness, it *yields* some.  `ChiLedger.lean` §N14 carries
52	`Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)` — "`[κ(P):k] < ∞`" — as an explicit binder on roughly
53	twenty statements across the lane, describing it as "the gated keystone input, not re-proved
54	here".  Approximation by constants makes `κ(P)` spanned by the single class of `1`, hence
55	finitely generated: `finite_localStepTgt_one_of_hasRationalResidues`, and on curve hypotheses
56	`finite_localStepTgt_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve`.
57	
58	That is why nothing in §3–§4 below carries a finiteness binder, including
59	`residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve`: the binder is discharged internally rather than
60	passed to the caller.  It is deliberately **not** registered as a global instance — see the
61	diamond note below, and note that a global instance would fire during synthesis inside every
62	lane statement and pin the `k`-action there.
63	
64	## The closedness input
65	
66	`residueFieldIsoBase` needs `IsClosed {P.point}`.  For a prime divisor this is *not* an
67	extra assumption: `Adelic/FiniteMapToP1.lean` proves
68	`isClosed_singleton_of_coheight_le_one`, and a prime divisor has `coheight = 1` by
69	definition while the generic point has coheight `0` on a curve.  `isClosed_primeDivisor`
70	below packages this, taking the one-dimensionality of the curve as the hypothesis
71	`hdim` that the sibling file also uses.
72	
73	## Main declarations
74	
75	* `stalkStructureHom_eq_constMap_germ`, `algebraMap_stalk_functionField`,
76	  `isScalarTower_stalk_functionField` — the compatibility layer (item 1–2 above).
77	* `bijective_residue_comp_stalkStructureHom` — `k → 𝒪_P → κ(P)` is **bijective** at a
78	  closed point, from mathlib's `residueFieldIsoBase`.
79	* `hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve` — `HasRationalResidues k P`, **discharged**:
80	  every function regular at `P` agrees with a constant to first order.
81	* `finite_localStepTgt_one_of_hasRationalResidues`,
82	  `finite_localStepTgt_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve` — the **N14 finiteness gate**, discharged.
83	* `residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve` — `[κ(P):k] = 1`, the campaign's residue fact,
84	  with no finiteness binder.
85	* `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_isAlgClosed_curve` — the **unweighted** principal-degree-zero
86	  statement, from the ledger, with the residue input now discharged rather than assumed.
87	
88	## A note on an instance diamond (read before adding imports here)
89	
90	With `Picard/TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra.lean` imported, `open scoped AlgebraicGeometry`
91	brings in `overStalkAlgebra C x : Algebra k 𝒪_{C,x}`.  At `x = genericPoint C.left` its
92	target `𝒪_{C,generic}` *is* `K(C)` by definition, so it competes with
93	`Scheme.functionFieldAlgebra` for `Algebra k K(C)` — and the two are **not**
94	definitionally equal (machine-checked: `rfl` fails).  Everything below therefore opens
95	only `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`, and constructs the stalk algebra as an explicit `letI`
96	rather than by activating the scoped instance.  Activating it would silently re-pin
97	`sectionSub`/`orderGeSub`/`residueDeg` to a different `k`-action than the rest of the
98	lane uses.
99	-/
100	
101	set_option autoImplicit false
102	
103	universe u
104	
105	open CategoryTheory Limits IsDedekindDomain
106	open scoped WithZero AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
107	
108	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
109	namespace Adelic
110	
111	/-! ## §1. The stalk `k`-algebra and its compatibility with `K(C)` -/
112	
113	section StalkAlgebra
114	
115	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
116	
117	/-- **The structure homomorphism into a stalk factors through the global sections.**
118	`k → 𝒪_{C,x}` is `constMap C : k → Γ(C,⊤)` followed by the germ at `x`.
119	
120	Both sides are the stalk map of `C.hom` precomposed with `ΓSpecIso.inv`; mathlib's
121	`Hom.germ_stalkMap` is exactly the statement that the germ commutes past a stalk map.
122	This is the lemma that ties `Picard/TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra.lean`'s stalk algebra to
123	`Adelic/GateInstances.lean`'s function-field algebra, which is built from `constMap`. -/
124	theorem stalkStructureHom_eq_constMap_germ (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
125	    (x : C.left) :
126	    stalkStructureHom C.hom x
127	      = Scheme.constMap C ≫ C.left.presheaf.germ ⊤ x trivial := by
128	  rw [stalkStructureHom, Scheme.constMap, Category.assoc]
129	  congr 1
130	  exact C.hom.germ_stalkMap ⊤ x trivial
131	
132	/-- **The two `k`-algebra structures agree.**  The image of a constant `c : k` in `K(C)`
133	is the same whether one goes `k → 𝒪_P → K(C)` (through `stalkStructureHom`) or directly
134	`k → K(C)` (through `Scheme.functionFieldAlgebra`).
135	
136	This is what makes the stalk-level argument of §2 usable in the order language of the
137	adelic lane, whose `algebraMap k K(X)` is the latter.  Proof: rewrite the stalk map as
138	`constMap ≫ germ` (`stalkStructureHom_eq_constMap_germ`), then both sides are
139	`algebraMap Γ(C,⊤) K(C) ∘ constMap` — the first by mathlib's
140	`functionField_isScalarTower`, the second by `Scheme.algebraMap_functionField_eq`. -/
141	theorem algebraMap_stalk_functionField (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
142	    [IsIntegral C.left] (x : C.left) (c : k) :
143	    algebraMap (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) C.left.functionField
144	        ((stalkStructureHom C.hom x).hom c)
145	      = algebraMap k C.left.functionField c := by
146	  haveI : Nonempty (⊤ : C.left.Opens) := Scheme.nonempty_top_opens C.left
147	  letI : Algebra ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) :=
148	    C.left.presheaf.algebra_section_stalk (⟨x, trivial⟩ : (⊤ : C.left.Opens))
149	  haveI : IsScalarTower ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk x)
150	      C.left.functionField :=
151	    functionField_isScalarTower C.left ⊤ ⟨x, trivial⟩
152	  have h1 : (stalkStructureHom C.hom x).hom c
153	      = algebraMap ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk x)
154	        ((Scheme.constMap C).hom c) := by
155	    rw [stalkStructureHom_eq_constMap_germ C x]; rfl
156	  rw [h1, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply]
157	  rfl
158	
159	/-- **The tower `k → 𝒪_P → K(C)`** — binder (2) of `GlobalGeneration.lean` §7, now built.
160	Immediate from `algebraMap_stalk_functionField`. -/
161	theorem isScalarTower_stalk_functionField (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
162	    [IsIntegral C.left] (x : C.left) :
163	    letI : Algebra k (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) := stalkAlgebra C.hom x
164	    IsScalarTower k (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) C.left.functionField := by
165	  letI : Algebra k (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) := stalkAlgebra C.hom x
166	  refine IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun c => ?_
167	  exact (algebraMap_stalk_functionField C x c).symm
168	
169	end StalkAlgebra
170	
171	/-! ## §2. `κ(P) = k` at a closed point, over an algebraically closed base
172	
173	Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.residueFieldIsoBase` gives `κ(x) ≅ k` as a `CommRingCat`
174	iso for a closed point of a scheme locally of finite type over an algebraically closed
175	`k`.  What is needed here is the *ring-map* form: that the composite
176	`k → 𝒪_x → κ(x)` — the map the order language sees — is bijective.  That follows once
177	the composite is identified with the iso's inverse, which is `residue_stalkStructureHom_eq`
178	below: an identity of `Spec`-morphisms, checked through `Spec.map_injective`. -/
179	
180	section ResidueBijective
181	
182	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
183	
184	/-- **A prime divisor of a curve is a closed point.**  On an irreducible scheme all of
185	whose points have coheight `≤ 1` (the curve condition, supplied by
186	`coheight_le_one_of_curve`), a point of coheight `1` is not the generic point — the
187	generic point has coheight `0` — hence is closed by
188	`isClosed_singleton_of_coheight_le_one` (`Adelic/FiniteMapToP1.lean`).
189	
190	This is why the closedness input of `residueFieldIsoBase` costs nothing here: it is part
191	of what `X.PrimeDivisor` already asserts. -/
192	theorem isClosed_primeDivisor {X : Scheme.{u}} [IrreducibleSpace X]
193	    (hdim : ∀ w : X, Order.coheight w ≤ 1) (P : X.PrimeDivisor) :
194	    IsClosed ({P.point} : Set X) := by
195	  refine isClosed_singleton_of_coheight_le_one hdim ?_
196	  intro hgen
197	  -- the generic point is maximal in the specialisation order, so has coheight `0`
198	  have hmax : IsMax (genericPoint X) := fun y hy => genericPoint_specializes y
199	  have h0 : Order.coheight P.point = 0 := by
200	    rw [hgen]; exact Order.IsMax.coheight_eq_zero hmax
201	  rw [P.coheight] at h0
202	  exact absurd h0 (by simp)
203	
204	/-- **Every non-generic point of a curve has coheight exactly one** — hence *is* a prime divisor.
205	
206	`coheight_le_one_of_curve` (`Adelic/FiniteMapToP1.lean`) gives `≤ 1` from smoothness.  The
207	reverse needs only that a non-generic point is not maximal in the specialisation order: the
208	generic point satisfies `P ≤ genericPoint` always (mathlib's convention is
209	`x ≤ y ↔ y ⤳ x`, and the generic point specialises to everything), so if `P` were maximal it
210	would satisfy `genericPoint ≤ P` too and antisymmetry would force `P = genericPoint`.
211	
212	**Why this is worth having as a theorem.** `X.PrimeDivisor` bundles a point with a proof that
213	its coheight is `1`, and until now AJC had no way to *produce* one on a curve:
214	`Scheme.WeilDivisor.ofClosedPoint` case-splits on `Order.coheight P = 1` and falls back to the
215	zero divisor when it cannot be shown, so every statement quantified over `X.PrimeDivisor` was
216	formally at risk of being vacuous.  `primeDivisorOfNotGeneric` below removes that risk. -/
217	theorem coheight_eq_one_of_ne_genericPoint (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
218	    [IrreducibleSpace C.left] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
219	    {x : C.left} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint C.left) :
220	    Order.coheight x = 1 := by
221	  refine le_antisymm (coheight_le_one_of_curve C x) ?_
222	  -- `x` is not maximal (the generic point strictly dominates it), so its coheight is not `0`
223	  have hnotmax : ¬ IsMax x := by
224	    intro hmax
225	    exact hx ((genericPoint_specializes x).antisymm
226	      (hmax (genericPoint_specializes x))).symm.eq
227	  have hne : Order.coheight x ≠ 0 := fun h => hnotmax (Order.coheight_eq_zero.mp h)
228	  exact Order.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr hne
229	
230	/-- **A non-generic point of a curve, packaged as a prime divisor.**  The producer that makes
231	every `∀ P : C.left.PrimeDivisor` statement in this lane non-vacuous. -/
232	def primeDivisorOfNotGeneric (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
233	    [IrreducibleSpace C.left] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
234	    {x : C.left} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint C.left) :
235	    C.left.PrimeDivisor :=
236	  ⟨x, coheight_eq_one_of_ne_genericPoint C hx⟩
237	
238	/-- **The composite `k → 𝒪_x → κ(x)` is the inverse of mathlib's `residueFieldIsoBase`.**
239	
240	Both are morphisms `k ⟶ κ(x)` in `CommRingCat`; `Spec` is faithful, so it suffices to
241	check the induced `Spec` morphisms agree, and there both sides unfold to
242	`X.fromSpecResidueField x ≫ C.hom` — the left by `Scheme.fromSpecResidueField` plus
243	`fromSpecStalk_comp_eq` (`Picard/TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra.lean`), the right by mathlib's
244	`SpecMap_residueFieldIsoBase_inv`. -/
245	theorem residue_stalkStructureHom_eq [IsAlgClosed k]
246	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom]
247	    (x : C.left) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set C.left)) :
248	    stalkStructureHom C.hom x ≫ C.left.residue x
249	      = (residueFieldIsoBase C.hom x hx).inv := by
250	  apply Spec.map_injective
251	  rw [SpecMap_residueFieldIsoBase_inv, Spec.map_comp, Scheme.fromSpecResidueField,
252	    ← fromSpecStalk_comp_eq, Category.assoc]
253	
254	/-- **`k → κ(x)` is bijective at a closed point of a curve over an algebraically closed
255	base.**  Immediate from `residue_stalkStructureHom_eq`: an iso of `CommRingCat` has
256	bijective underlying ring map.
257	
258	This is the statement that replaces `GlobalScheme`'s three-binder route: no
259	`Module.Finite k κ_P` gate is consumed, because mathlib obtains integrality of `κ(x)` over
260	`k` from `LocallyOfFiniteType` through the Jacobson-space finiteness criterion. -/
261	theorem bijective_residue_comp_stalkStructureHom [IsAlgClosed k]
262	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom]
263	    (x : C.left) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set C.left)) :
264	    Function.Bijective
265	      ((C.left.residue x).hom.comp (stalkStructureHom C.hom x).hom) := by
266	  have h : (C.left.residue x).hom.comp (stalkStructureHom C.hom x).hom
267	      = (residueFieldIsoBase C.hom x hx).inv.hom := by
268	    rw [← residue_stalkStructureHom_eq C x hx]; rfl
269	  rw [h]
270	  exact (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective
271	    (residueFieldIsoBase C.hom x hx).inv).mp inferInstance
272	
273	/-- **Every stalk element is a constant modulo the maximal ideal.**  The surjectivity half
274	of `bijective_residue_comp_stalkStructureHom`, restated as the approximation statement on
275	the stalk: for `a ∈ 𝒪_x` there is `c : k` with `a − c ∈ 𝔪_x`. -/
276	theorem exists_const_sub_mem_maximalIdeal [IsAlgClosed k]
277	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom]
278	    (x : C.left) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set C.left))
279	    (a : C.left.presheaf.stalk x) :
280	    ∃ c : k, a - (stalkStructureHom C.hom x).hom c ∈
281	      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) := by
282	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := (bijective_residue_comp_stalkStructureHom C x hx).surjective
283	    ((C.left.residue x).hom a)
284	  rw [RingHom.comp_apply] at hc
285	  refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
286	  rw [← IsLocalRing.residue_eq_zero_iff]
287	  change (C.left.residue x).hom _ = 0
288	  rw [map_sub, hc, sub_self]
289	
290	end ResidueBijective
291	
292	/-! ## §3. `HasRationalResidues`, discharged
293	
294	The stalk statement of §2 is now translated into the order language of the adelic lane.
295	The translation has two steps and both are already available:
296	
297	* `f` with `ord_P f ≥ 0` lifts to `a ∈ 𝒪_P` — `exists_stalk_lift_of_order_nonneg`
298	  (`ChiLedger.lean` §N14b);
299	* `a − c ∈ 𝔪_P` becomes `ord_P (f − c) ≥ 1` — `mem_orderGe_one_iff_mem_maximalIdeal`
300	  (`GlobalGeneration.lean` §7), whose statement is phrased on `orderGe P 1` rather than on
301	  the raw inequality precisely so that `f = c` is admitted (the project's `ord_P 0 = 0`
302	  convention would make the inequality form false there).
303	
304	The `k`-action bookkeeping is `algebraMap_stalk_functionField` (§1): the constant produced
305	on the stalk and the constant the order language expects are the same element of `K(C)`. -/
306	
307	section Discharge
308	
309	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
310	
311	/-- **`HasRationalResidues` holds at every prime divisor of a curve over an algebraically
312	closed field** — the residue fact of the campaign, now a theorem on AJC's own curve
313	hypotheses rather than on unbuilt stalk binders.
314	
315	Compare `hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed` (`GlobalGeneration.lean` §7), which proves the
316	same conclusion but from `[Algebra k 𝒪_P]`, `[IsScalarTower k 𝒪_P K(X)]` and
317	`[Module.Finite k κ_P]`, none of which AJC constructs.  Here the first two are built (§1)
318	and the third is not needed (§2). -/
319	theorem hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
320	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
321	    [IsLocallyNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
322	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
323	    (P : C.left.PrimeDivisor) :
324	    HasRationalResidues k P := by
325	  intro f hf
326	  rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hf0
327	  · refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
328	    rw [map_zero, sub_zero]
329	    exact (orderGe P 1).zero_mem
330	  -- lift `f` to the stalk
331	  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := exists_stalk_lift_of_order_nonneg hf0
332	    ((mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero hf0).mp hf)
333	  -- `P.point` is a closed point of the curve, so `κ(P) = k`
334	  have hclosed : IsClosed ({P.point} : Set C.left) :=
335	    isClosed_primeDivisor (coheight_le_one_of_curve C) P
336	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := exists_const_sub_mem_maximalIdeal C P.point hclosed a
337	  refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
338	  have himg := (mem_orderGe_one_iff_mem_maximalIdeal P
339	    (a - (stalkStructureHom C.hom P.point).hom c)).mpr hc
340	  rw [map_sub, ha, algebraMap_stalk_functionField C P.point c] at himg
341	  exact himg
342	
343	/-! ### The N14 residue-finiteness gate is discharged too
344	
345	`Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)` — "`[κ(P):k] < ∞`" — is carried as an instance binder
346	by roughly twenty statements across the adelic lane, and `ChiLedger.lean` §N14 describes it
347	as "the gated keystone input, not re-proved here".  It is now **provable** on curve
348	hypotheses, and cheaply, because `hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve` above needs no
349	finiteness at all: approximation by constants says every class in the quotient is a
350	`k`-multiple of the class of `1`, so the quotient is spanned by a *single* vector.
351	
352	This is why §3 is ordered the way it is.  Proving `residueDeg k P = 1` through
353	`residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues` would require the finiteness binder, since that
354	equivalence carries it; deriving finiteness from the approximation statement *first* removes
355	the binder from everything downstream, including `residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve`
356	itself. -/
357	
358	/-- **The residue field is finite-dimensional, from approximation by constants alone.**
359	If every function regular at `P` agrees with a constant to first order, then
360	`κ(P) = orderGe P 0 ⧸ orderGe P 1` is spanned by the class of `1`, hence finitely generated.
361	
362	Stated on `HasRationalResidues` rather than on curve hypotheses so that it is reusable: this
363	is the general fact that the approximation statement is *strictly stronger* than the
364	finiteness gate N14 assumes.  The spanning computation is the one in the `←` branch of
365	`residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues`; here it is used for finiteness rather than for
366	the rank bound. -/
367	theorem finite_localStepTgt_one_of_hasRationalResidues
368	    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
369	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X] [Algebra k X.functionField]
370	    [IsConstantField k X] (P : X.PrimeDivisor)
371	    (happrox : HasRationalResidues k P) :
372	    Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1) := by
373	  have hone : (1 : X.functionField) ∈ orderGeSub k P (1 - 1) := by
374	    rw [mem_orderGeSub]
375	    exact Or.inr (by rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_one]; norm_num)
376	  -- every class is a `k`-multiple of the class of `1`
377	  have hspan : (⊤ : Submodule k (localStepTgt k P 1)) ≤
378	      Submodule.span k {Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.comap
379	        (orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)).subtype (orderGeSub k P 1)) ⟨1, hone⟩} := by
380	    intro z _
381	    obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ z
382	    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := happrox (g : X.functionField)
383	      (by
384	        have hg2 := g.2
385	        rw [mem_orderGeSub] at hg2
386	        exact orderGe_antitone (by norm_num) hg2)
387	    rw [Submodule.mem_span_singleton]
388	    refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
389	    rw [← Submodule.Quotient.mk_smul, Submodule.Quotient.eq, Submodule.mem_comap,
390	      Submodule.subtype_apply]
391	    have hval : ((c • ⟨1, hone⟩ - g : orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)) :
392	        X.functionField) = -(g - algebraMap k X.functionField c) := by
393	      change c • (1 : X.functionField) - (g : X.functionField) = _
394	      rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_one]
395	      ring
396	    rw [mem_orderGeSub, hval]
397	    exact (orderGe P 1).neg_mem hc
398	  -- a module whose `⊤` sits inside a one-vector span is finitely generated
399	  have htop : (⊤ : Submodule k (localStepTgt k P 1))
400	      = Submodule.span k {Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.comap
401	        (orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)).subtype (orderGeSub k P 1)) ⟨1, hone⟩} :=
402	    le_antisymm hspan le_top
403	  exact Module.Finite.of_fg_top (htop ▸ Submodule.fg_span_singleton _)
404	
405	/-- **The N14 residue-finiteness gate, discharged on curve hypotheses.**
406	`[κ(P):k] < ∞` at every prime divisor of a curve over an algebraically closed base.
407	
408	Not registered as a global instance: the lane's statements take it as an explicit binder and
409	a global instance here would change which `k`-action they synthesize against (see the diamond
410	note in the module docstring).  Consumers should apply it explicitly, or `haveI` it. -/
411	theorem finite_localStepTgt_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
412	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
413	    [IsLocallyNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
414	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
415	    (P : C.left.PrimeDivisor) :
416	    Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1) :=
417	  finite_localStepTgt_one_of_hasRationalResidues P
418	    (hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve C P)
419	
420	/-- **The residue degree is one** at every prime divisor of a curve over an algebraically
421	closed base: `[κ(P) : k] = 1`.
422	
423	This is the fact that `SectionBounds.lean` §4 and `GlobalGeneration.lean` §5–§7 both reduce
424	to and both leave open.  It closes item 1 of the two-item residue list in
425	`SectionBounds.lean` §4.
426	
427	Note there is **no finiteness binder**: it is supplied internally by
428	`finite_localStepTgt_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve`, so this statement's hypotheses are the curve
429	hypotheses and nothing else. -/
430	theorem residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
431	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
432	    [IsLocallyNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
433	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
434	    (P : C.left.PrimeDivisor) :
435	    residueDeg k P = 1 :=
436	  haveI := finite_localStepTgt_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve C P
437	  (residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues k P).mpr
438	    (hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve C P)
439	
440	/-! ### The consequences, with the residue input no longer a hypothesis
441	
442	`GlobalGeneration.lean` §6 draws two conclusions from `HasRationalResidues` — uniform global
443	generation with threshold `b + 1`, and the unweighted principal-degree-zero statement — but
444	carries it as a hypothesis `hres`.  §3 above discharges `hres` on curve hypotheses, so both
445	conclusions can be restated with **one** open input instead of two.
446	
447	Read the remaining hypothesis carefully: `hledger` is the closed χ-ledger, and it is *still*
448	not a theorem in this project.  `Adelic/LedgerClosure.lean` proves it on the whole effective
449	cone from the one-point bump (`chi_eq_of_bump_of_nonneg`) and states the remaining half
450	exactly as an `iff` (`chi_eq_iff_step_of_bump`); the negative part needs an input the lane
451	does not have.  So what follows is a genuine reduction from two open inputs to one, not a
452	discharge of the leaf. -/
453	
454	/-- **The weighted degree is the geometric degree on a curve over an algebraically closed
455	base.**  `deg_k = deg`, with the residue-degree-one input discharged rather than assumed.
456	
457	This is what makes the adelic lane's weighted statements into statements about the geometric
458	`Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree` that the rest of the project uses. -/
459	theorem degK_eq_degree_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
460	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
461	    [IsNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
462	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
463	    (D : C.left.WeilDivisor) :
464	    degK k D = Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree D :=
465	  degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one k
466	    (fun P _ => residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve C P)
467	
468	/-- **Principal divisors have geometric degree zero on a curve over an algebraically closed
469	base, given the closed ledger** — the adelic route to the open leaf
470	`Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`, now resting on the **ledger alone**.
471	
472	Compare `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_hasRationalResidues` (`GlobalGeneration.lean` §6),
473	which takes both the ledger *and* the approximation statement.  The second hypothesis is
474	gone here.
475	
476	This is the sharpest honest form of the leaf reachable today.  It is deliberately **not**
477	substituted into `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`, whose statement mentions no
478	hypotheses: doing so would make a hypothesis-free theorem depend silently on the ledger. -/
479	theorem degree_principal_eq_zero_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
480	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
481	    [IsNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
482	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
483	    (U₀ U₁ : C.left.Opens)
484	    (hledger : ∀ D : C.left.WeilDivisor,
485	      chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
486	    {g : C.left.functionField} (hg : g ≠ 0) :
487	    Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree (Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg) = 0 :=
488	  degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one k U₀ U₁ hledger hg
489	    (fun P _ => residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve C P)
490	
491	/-- **Uniform global generation with threshold `b + 1`**, with the residue input discharged.
492	Above weighted degree `b`, `𝒪(D)` is generated by global sections at *every* prime divisor,
493	the residue-degree bound being `r = 1` on a curve over an algebraically closed base.
494	
495	Still single-field, and still conditional on the ledger, the base vanishing and the peel —
496	see the three-gap discussion in `BoundedVanishing.lean`. -/
497	theorem exists_bound_forall_generatedAt_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
498	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
499	    [IsNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
500	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
501	    [∀ D : C.left.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k ⊤ D)]
502	    (U₀ U₁ : C.left.Opens)
503	    (hledger : ∀ D : C.left.WeilDivisor,
504	      chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
505	    (D₀ : C.left.WeilDivisor) (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D₀))
506	    (hpeel : ∀ D' : C.left.WeilDivisor,
507	      (∀ P : C.left.PrimeDivisor, (show C.left.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P ≤
508	        (show C.left.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) →
509	      Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D') :
510	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : C.left.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D →
511	      ∀ P : C.left.PrimeDivisor, GeneratedAt k D P :=
512	  haveI : ∀ P : C.left.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1) :=
513	    fun P => finite_localStepTgt_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve C P
514	  exists_bound_forall_generatedAt k U₀ U₁ hledger D₀ hbase hpeel 1
515	    (fun P => le_of_eq (residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve C P))
516	
517	/-- **The threshold conclusions are not vacuous, unconditionally on a curve.**  For every bound
518	`b` and every prime divisor `P`, some multiple `n·P` has weighted degree `≥ b`.
519	
520	`exists_degK_ge` (`BoundedVanishing.lean`) proves this but carries the residue-finiteness
521	binder; here it is discharged, so the non-vacuity of every `∃ b, ∀ D, b ≤ deg_k D → …`
522	conclusion in the lane is unconditional on curve hypotheses.  Worth having as a statement
523	rather than a remark: that quantifier shape is exactly the one that *can* be satisfied
524	trivially, and a reader is entitled to see it ruled out. -/
525	theorem exists_degK_ge_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
526	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
527	    [IsNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
528	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
529	    (b : ℤ) (P : C.left.PrimeDivisor) :
530	    ∃ n : ℕ, b ≤ degK k ((n : ℤ) • pointDivisor P : C.left.WeilDivisor) :=
531	  haveI := finite_localStepTgt_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve C P
532	  exists_degK_ge k b P
533	
534	/-! ### Riemann–Roch in the vanishing range, on the geometric degree
535	
536	The lane's numerical conclusions are all stated on the residue-weighted `deg_k`, because that
537	is what the χ-ledger telescopes to.  On a curve over an algebraically closed base the two
538	degrees agree (`degK_eq_degree_of_isAlgClosed_curve`), so those conclusions can be restated on
539	`Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree` — the invariant the rest of the project, and the classical
540	statement, use.
541	
542	`ell_eq_of_bound_degree` below is the `ℓ(D) = χ(0) + deg D` form; with `χ(0) = 1 − g` it is the
543	classical `ℓ(D) = deg D + 1 − g` for `deg D` large.  Note it is *not* free of the lane's open
544	inputs: it is `exists_bound_ell_eq` with the degree translated, so the ledger, the base
545	vanishing and the peel are all still there.  What the translation removes is only the
546	residue-weighting, which was never an open input but was an obstacle to *quoting* the result. -/
547	
548	/-- **The Riemann inequality on the geometric degree.**  `deg D + χ(0) ≤ ℓ(D)` for every
549	divisor on a curve over an algebraically closed base, given the closed ledger.  The weighted
550	form is `degK_add_chi_zero_le_ell`; here the weighting is discharged. -/
551	theorem degree_add_chi_zero_le_ell_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
552	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
553	    [IsNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
554	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
555	    (U₀ U₁ : C.left.Opens)
556	    (hledger : ∀ D : C.left.WeilDivisor,
557	      chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
558	    (D : C.left.WeilDivisor) :
559	    Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree D + chi k U₀ U₁ 0 ≤ (ell k D : ℤ) := by
560	  rw [← degK_eq_degree_of_isAlgClosed_curve C D]
561	  exact degK_add_chi_zero_le_ell k U₀ U₁ hledger D
562	
563	/-- **Riemann–Roch in the vanishing range, on the geometric degree.**  There is a threshold
564	past which `ℓ(D) = χ(0) + deg D` — an equality, not merely the Riemann inequality — for every
565	divisor of large geometric degree on a curve over an algebraically closed base.
566	
567	With `χ(0) = 1 − g` this is the classical `ℓ(D) = deg D + 1 − g`.  The threshold is stated on
568	`deg` rather than `deg_k` because the two coincide here.
569	
570	Conditional on the lane's three inputs (closed ledger, base vanishing, peel) exactly as
571	`exists_bound_ell_eq` is; the residue-weighting is what has been discharged, not those. -/
572	theorem exists_bound_ell_eq_degree_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
573	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
574	    [IsNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
575	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
576	    (U₀ U₁ : C.left.Opens)
577	    (hledger : ∀ D : C.left.WeilDivisor,
578	      chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
579	    (D₀ : C.left.WeilDivisor) (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D₀))
580	    (hpeel : ∀ D' : C.left.WeilDivisor,
581	      (∀ P : C.left.PrimeDivisor, (show C.left.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P ≤
582	        (show C.left.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) →
583	      Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D') :
584	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : C.left.WeilDivisor, b ≤ Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree D →
585	      (ell k D : ℤ) = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree D := by
586	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := exists_bound_ell_eq k U₀ U₁ hledger D₀ hbase hpeel
587	  refine ⟨b, fun D hD => ?_⟩
588	  rw [← degK_eq_degree_of_isAlgClosed_curve C D] at hD ⊢
589	  exact hb D hD
590	
591	end Discharge
592	
593	/-! ## §5. Extension uniformity: the statement, at last written down
594	
595	The lane's docstrings (`BoundedVanishing.lean`, `GlobalGeneration.lean` §"three gaps",
596	`SectionBounds.lean` §"What is NOT proved here") record gap (2), **extension uniformity**, as
597	not merely unproved but *not statable*: "the invariants here are pinned on a chosen 2-affine
598	cover, and `RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean` does not transport that cover to `C_κ`".  A
599	memory note to the same effect warned against re-planning it wrongly.
600	
601	**That is too strong, and this section corrects it.**  `CurveBaseChange.lean` §3 *does*
602	transport a cover: `AffineCoverMVSquare.baseChangeField` produces a bundled 2-affine cover of
603	`C_κ` from one of `C`, and its `U₁`/`U₂` are ordinary `Opens`, which is what `chi`, `ell`,
604	`h1dim` and `H1Mod` consume.  Together with the `κ`-algebra on `K(C_κ)` and the
605	`IsConstantField` gate — both available from `GateInstances.lean` applied to
606	`Scheme.baseChangeField C κ`, whose curve instances `CurveBaseChange.lean` §2 supplies — the
607	uniformity predicate can be written down.  `UniformlyBoundedVanishing` below does that.
608	
609	So the honest status of gap (2) is: **statable, and open**.  That is a weaker claim than
610	"proved" and a stronger one than "not statable", and the distinction matters because the two
611	call for different next steps — the second says build cover transport first, the first says the
612	transport exists and what is missing is the mathematics of flat base change for the invariants.
613	
614	What is genuinely missing, stated as precisely as I can:
615	
616	* `ℓ`, `h¹` and `χ` are `κ`-dimensions on `C_κ` and `k`-dimensions on `C`.  Uniformity needs
617	  them *compared*, which is flat base change for the section spaces —
618	  `Γ(C_κ, 𝒪(D_κ)) ≃ Γ(C, 𝒪(D)) ⊗_k κ` — and no such comparison exists in this project.
619	* Even the divisor correspondence is missing: `D ↦ D_κ` requires pulling a Weil divisor back
620	  along `C_κ ⟶ C`, and prime divisors need not stay prime (a closed point can split).  There is
621	  no `WeilDivisor` pullback in AJC.
622	
623	Neither is a cover-transport problem.  Recording the predicate without either of them is
624	deliberate: it makes the gap a statement someone can attack, rather than a paragraph asserting
625	it cannot be written.
626	-/
627	
628	section Uniformity
629	
630	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
631	
632	/-- **The extension-uniform bounded-vanishing predicate** — cluster P's gap (2), written down.
633	
634	`UniformlyBoundedVanishing C S` says: there is a **single** threshold `b`, independent of the
635	extension, such that for every field extension `κ/k` and every Weil divisor `D` of the
636	base-changed curve `C_κ` with `deg_κ D ≥ b`, the cover cohomology `Ȟ¹(D)` computed on the
637	base-changed cover `S_κ` vanishes.
638	
639	Contrast `exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod`, which fixes `k`, the cover and the base divisor:
640	there the bound may depend on all three.  Here `b` is chosen before `κ` is.
641	
642	This is a **definition, not a theorem** — nothing below proves it, and §5's docstring lists the
643	two genuinely missing inputs (flat base change for the section spaces, and a `WeilDivisor`
644	pullback along `C_κ ⟶ C`).  Its value is that the predicate typechecks, which the lane's
645	docstrings claimed it could not. -/
646	def UniformlyBoundedVanishing (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
647	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
648	    (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) : Prop :=
649	  ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ (κ : Type u) (_ : Field κ) (_ : Algebra k κ),
650	    ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.WeilDivisor,
651	      b ≤ degK κ D → Subsingleton
652	        (H1Mod κ (S.baseChangeField κ).U₁ (S.baseChangeField κ).U₂ D)
653	
654	/-! **One thing I could not state, recorded rather than papered over.**  The obvious sanity
655	check on the predicate — instantiate at `κ = k` and read off a single-field bound on `C_k` —
656	does not elaborate: it exceeds the `whnf` heartbeat limit, because supplying `Field k` and
657	`Algebra.id k` positionally forces Lean to unfold the base-change pullback and re-synthesise
658	the whole curve-instance tower inside `H1Mod`.  Raising `maxHeartbeats` would hide a real cost
659	rather than address it, and the natural fix — restating the predicate with `[Field κ]`
660	`[Algebra k κ]` as instance binders and quantifying over `κ` alone — changes the predicate's
661	shape, so I have left the definition as the faithful `∀ (κ) (_ : Field κ) (_ : Algebra k κ)`
662	form and recorded the limitation here.
663	
664	So the predicate typechecks but is not yet *convenient*: nothing has been instantiated at any
665	particular `κ`, including the trivial one.  A consumer should expect to spend effort on the
666	instance plumbing before using it. -/
667	
668	end Uniformity
669	
670	end Adelic
671	end AlgebraicGeometry
672

6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.ChiLedger
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SectionRingUniversal
9	
10	/-!
11	# Discharge of the adelic `IsConstantField` gate (campaign P-cluster opener)
12	
13	The χ-ledger of `RiemannRoch/Adelic/ChiLedger.lean` runs over a base field of
14	constants `k ↪ K(X)` packaged by the gate class `Adelic.IsConstantField k X`:
15	*every nonzero constant has order `0` at every prime divisor*.  The W1-F audit
16	dossier (run 0020) flagged this gate as instance-free and absent from the
17	campaign gate table.  This file discharges it for the situation the campaign
18	actually uses: a curve `C : Over (Spec k)` with the `k`-algebra structure on the
19	function field induced by the structure morphism.
20	
21	## Statement audit (BLOCKING house rule; verdict recorded before proving)
22	
23	* The gate `IsConstantField k X` asserts only the **easy direction** of the
24	  field-of-constants dialectic: nonzero constants are everywhere units, i.e.
25	  `ord_P (c) = 0` for `c ∈ k^×`.  With the algebra structure factoring through
26	  `k → Γ(C, 𝒪_C) → 𝒪_{C,P} → K(C)`, this is TRUE at full generality: a nonzero
27	  `c` is a unit in the field `k`, ring maps preserve units, so its image in the
28	  DVR stalk `𝒪_{C,P}` is a unit, and `Ring.ordFrac` of a stalk unit is `1`
29	  (Mathlib `Ring.ordFrac_of_isUnit`), i.e. `ord_P = 0`.  **No properness, no

10	/-!
11	# Discharge of the adelic `IsConstantField` gate (campaign P-cluster opener)
12	
13	The χ-ledger of `RiemannRoch/Adelic/ChiLedger.lean` runs over a base field of
14	constants `k ↪ K(X)` packaged by the gate class `Adelic.IsConstantField k X`:
15	*every nonzero constant has order `0` at every prime divisor*.  The W1-F audit
16	dossier (run 0020) flagged this gate as instance-free and absent from the
17	campaign gate table.  This file discharges it for the situation the campaign
18	actually uses: a curve `C : Over (Spec k)` with the `k`-algebra structure on the
19	function field induced by the structure morphism.
20	
21	## Statement audit (BLOCKING house rule; verdict recorded before proving)
22	
23	* The gate `IsConstantField k X` asserts only the **easy direction** of the
24	  field-of-constants dialectic: nonzero constants are everywhere units, i.e.
25	  `ord_P (c) = 0` for `c ∈ k^×`.  With the algebra structure factoring through
26	  `k → Γ(C, 𝒪_C) → 𝒪_{C,P} → K(C)`, this is TRUE at full generality: a nonzero
27	  `c` is a unit in the field `k`, ring maps preserve units, so its image in the
28	  DVR stalk `𝒪_{C,P}` is a unit, and `Ring.ordFrac` of a stalk unit is `1`
29	  (Mathlib `Ring.ordFrac_of_isUnit`), i.e. `ord_P = 0`.  **No properness, no
30	  geometric integrality, no `B0` input is needed** — only `[IsIntegral C.left]`
31	  (for the function-field formalism) plus the standing `(*)`-hypotheses
32	  `[IsLocallyNoetherian]`, `[IsRegularInCodimensionOne]` of the `order` API.
33	* The W1-F dossier proposed discharging the gate "via B0's
34	  `globalSectionsAlgEquivBase`".  Correction (this file): `B0`/
35	  `HasTrivialConstants` is the content of the **converse** direction — that
36	  every everywhere-regular function is a constant, `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k` — which the
37	  gate does *not* assert.  `B0` enters only as the natural home of the ring map
38	  `constMap C : k → Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` used to *define* the algebra structure
39	  (`functionFieldAlgebra` below); that map exists for every `C : Over (Spec k)`.
40	* Instance-diamond audit: Mathlib has **no** `Algebra k X.functionField`
41	  instance for a plain field `k` (only `Algebra Γ(X, U) X.functionField` and
42	  `Algebra (𝒪_{X,x}) X.functionField`), so `functionFieldAlgebra` creates no
43	  diamond.  It is `scoped` (house pattern of
44	  `Scheme.globalSectionsAlgebra`, `Picard/SectionRingUniversal.lean`) — the
45	  χ-ledger consumer opens `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme` to activate it together
46	  with the gate instance.
47	
48	## Main declarations
49	
50	* `Scheme.RationalMap.order_algebraMap_eq_zero_of_isUnit` — reusable brick: the
51	  order of (the image in `K(X)` of) a stalk unit at a prime divisor is `0`.
52	* `Scheme.functionFieldAlgebra` — the `k`-algebra structure on `K(C)` induced by
53	  the structure morphism, through `constMap` and the germ at the generic point.
54	* `Scheme.instIsConstantField` — the gate discharge.
55	
56	Campaign reference: wave-2 P-cluster opener (task A) of
57	`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`; W1-F dossier §7 gate inventory.
58	-/
59	
60	universe u
61	
62	open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry
63	
64	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
65	
66	/-- **Order of a stalk unit is zero.**  For a prime divisor `Y` of a scheme `X`
67	satisfying the standing `(*)`-hypotheses, and a *unit* `u` of the DVR stalk
68	`𝒪_{X,Y}`, the order of vanishing of its image in the function field is `0`:
69	units have neither zeros nor poles along `Y`.  Wrapper around Mathlib's
70	`Ring.ordFrac_of_isUnit` through the definition
71	`order Y f = WithZero.log (Ring.ordFrac 𝒪_{X,Y} f)`. -/
72	theorem Scheme.RationalMap.order_algebraMap_eq_zero_of_isUnit
73	    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
74	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X] (Y : X.PrimeDivisor)
75	    {u : X.presheaf.stalk Y.point} (hu : IsUnit u) :
76	    Scheme.RationalMap.order Y
77	      (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk Y.point) X.functionField u) = 0 := by
78	  unfold Scheme.RationalMap.order
79	  rw [Ring.ordFrac_of_isUnit hu, WithZero.log_one]
80	
81	namespace Scheme
82	
83	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
84	
85	/-- The total open `⊤` of an irreducible (e.g. integral) scheme is nonempty —
86	instance form, so that instance heads mentioning the Mathlib
87	`Algebra Γ(X, ⊤) X.functionField` (which carries a `[Nonempty ⊤]` binder) can
88	synthesize.  Scoped to avoid polluting general `Nonempty` searches. -/
89	scoped instance nonempty_top_opens (X : Scheme.{u}) [IrreducibleSpace X] :
90	    Nonempty (⊤ : X.Opens) :=
91	  ⟨⟨genericPoint X, trivial⟩⟩
92	
93	/-- The `k`-algebra structure on the function field `K(C)` of an integral
94	`k`-scheme `C`, induced by the structure morphism: the composite
95	`k → Γ(C, 𝒪_C) → K(C)` of `constMap C` (`Picard/SectionRingUniversal.lean`)
96	with the germ at the generic point.  Scoped, mirroring
97	`globalSectionsAlgebra`. -/
98	noncomputable scoped instance functionFieldAlgebra
99	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left] :
100	    Algebra k C.left.functionField :=
101	  RingHom.toAlgebra ((C.left.germToFunctionField ⊤).hom.comp (constMap C).hom)
102	
103	/-- The `k`-algebra map to the function field factors through the global
104	sections: `algebraMap k K(C) = germToFunctionField ∘ constMap` — definitional
105	unfolding of `functionFieldAlgebra`, stated against the Mathlib
106	`Algebra Γ(C, ⊤) K(C)` instance. -/
107	lemma algebraMap_functionField_eq (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
108	    [IsIntegral C.left] :
109	    algebraMap k C.left.functionField
110	      = (algebraMap ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) C.left.functionField).comp (constMap C).hom :=
111	  rfl
112	
113	/-- The tower `k → Γ(C, 𝒪_C) → K(C)` of the structure-morphism algebra
114	structures. -/
115	scoped instance isScalarTower_globalSections_functionField
116	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left] :
117	    IsScalarTower k ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) C.left.functionField :=
118	  IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (algebraMap_functionField_eq C)
119	
120	/-- **The structure field satisfies the adelic `IsConstantField` interface.**
121	For an integral
122	`k`-scheme `C` satisfying the `(*)`-hypotheses, with the structure-morphism
123	algebra structure on `K(C)`, every nonzero constant `c ∈ k` has order `0` at
124	every prime divisor: `c` is a unit in the field `k`, hence its image in each
125	DVR stalk is a unit, and units have order `0`
126	(`order_algebraMap_eq_zero_of_isUnit`).
127	
128	Audit verdict (see module docstring): TRUE at this generality — no properness,
129	no `B0`/`HasTrivialConstants` input; this is the easy direction of the
130	field-of-constants dialectic. -/
131	theorem isConstantField_functionField (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
132	    [IsIntegral C.left] [IsLocallyNoetherian C.left]
133	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left] :
134	    Adelic.IsConstantField k C.left where
135	  order_algebraMap_eq_zero P c hc := by
136	    letI : Algebra ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk P.point) :=
137	      C.left.presheaf.algebra_section_stalk
138	        (⟨P.point, trivial⟩ : (⊤ : C.left.Opens))
139	    haveI : IsScalarTower ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk P.point)
140	        C.left.functionField :=
141	      functionField_isScalarTower C.left ⊤ ⟨P.point, trivial⟩
142	    have h1 : algebraMap k C.left.functionField c
143	        = algebraMap ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) C.left.functionField ((constMap C).hom c) := rfl
144	    have hu : IsUnit (algebraMap ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk P.point)
145	        ((constMap C).hom c)) :=
146	      ((isUnit_iff_ne_zero.mpr hc).map (constMap C).hom).map _
147	    rw [h1, IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤)
148	      (C.left.presheaf.stalk P.point) C.left.functionField]
149	    exact Scheme.RationalMap.order_algebraMap_eq_zero_of_isUnit P hu
150	
151	/-- Scoped instance form of `isConstantField_functionField`. -/
152	scoped instance instIsConstantField (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
153	    [IsIntegral C.left] [IsLocallyNoetherian C.left]
154	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left] :
155	    Adelic.IsConstantField k C.left :=
156	  isConstantField_functionField C
157	
158	end Scheme
159	
160	end AlgebraicGeometry

466	/-! ## §5. What `[κ(P):k] = 1` actually says
467	
468	Both the uniform generation statement (`r = 1`) and the open geometric leaf
469	`Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero` (through
470	`degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one`, `SectionBounds.lean` §4) reduce to the
471	single fact `residueDeg k P = 1`.  It has been carried as an informal remark — "over an
472	algebraically closed base every closed point has residue field `k̄`".  This section
473	replaces the remark by a **machine-checked equivalence** to a concrete, checkable
474	statement about rational functions:
475	
476	`residueDeg k P = 1 ↔ every function of order ≥ 0 at `P` agrees with a constant to
477	first order at `P`.`
478	
479	That is `residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues`.  It converts the remaining leaf from
480	a claim about residue fields — which in this substrate would require identifying
481	`localStepTgt k P 1` with `IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk P.point)`, an
482	identification this project does not have — into an approximation statement in the order
483	language the substrate already speaks.
484	
485	Note what is **not** claimed *in this section*: `HasRationalResidues` is not proved here for
486	an algebraically closed base.  Doing so needs the multiplicative structure of `κ(P)` (a
487	finite-dimensional *field* extension of an algebraically closed `k` is trivial —
488	`IsAlgClosed.algebraMap_bijective_of_isIntegral`), and `localStepTgt k P 1` is
489	constructed here as a quotient of `k`-submodules with no ring structure on it.  Finite
490	dimensionality alone does not give dimension one for a mere vector space, so the gap is
491	real and is exactly the missing ring-structure identification.
492	
493	**It is proved elsewhere now**, for a curve: `Adelic.hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve`
494	(`Adelic/ResidueField.lean`).  Note how it escapes the obstruction just described — it never
495	identifies `localStepTgt k P 1` with the stalk residue field.  It proves the *approximation
496	statement* directly, by lifting to the stalk and using that `k → κ_P` is onto there, and then
497	feeds it back through this section's equivalence to reach `residueDeg k P = 1`.  So the `iff`
498	above is what makes the discharge possible: the ring-structure identification is still absent,
499	and is still not needed.
500	-/
501	
502	section RationalResidues
503	
504	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
505	    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
506	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X]
507	
508	/-- **Every function regular at `P` agrees with a constant to first order.**
509	`∀ f` with `ord_P f ≥ 0`, some `c ∈ k` has `ord_P (f − c) ≥ 1`.
510	
511	This is the concrete content of "`κ(P) = k`", phrased in the order language rather than
512	through the residue field: the residue of `f` at `P` is the constant `c`.  Over an
513	algebraically closed base field it is the standard fact that a closed point of a curve
514	has residue field the base field; here it is an explicit hypothesis, and
515	`residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues` shows it is *exactly* equivalent to
516	`[κ(P):k] = 1`. -/
517	def HasRationalResidues (P : X.PrimeDivisor) : Prop :=
518	  ∀ f : X.functionField, f ∈ orderGe P 0 →
519	    ∃ c : k, f - algebraMap k X.functionField c ∈ orderGe P 1
520	
521	/-- **`[κ(P):k] = 1` is equivalent to first-order approximation by constants.**
522	
523	`→` The quotient `localStepTgt k P 1 = orderGe P 0 / orderGe P 1` has dimension one and
524	its class of `1` is nonzero (`nontrivial_localStepTgt_one`), hence spans; so the class of
525	any `f` is `c • [1] = [c]`, i.e. `f − c ∈ orderGe P 1`.
526	
527	`←` Conversely, approximation says every class is a `k`-multiple of `[1]`, so the
528	quotient is spanned by one vector and has dimension `≤ 1`; with `1 ≤ [κ(P):k]`
529	(`one_le_residueDeg`) it is exactly `1`.
530	
531	The `→` direction needs no finiteness instance; `←` produces one, since a space spanned
532	by a single vector is finite-dimensional. -/
533	theorem residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues (P : X.PrimeDivisor)
534	    [Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
535	    residueDeg k P = 1 ↔ HasRationalResidues k P := by
536	  have hone : (1 : X.functionField) ∈ orderGeSub k P (1 - 1) := by
537	    rw [mem_orderGeSub]
538	    exact Or.inr (by rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_one]; norm_num)
539	  constructor
540	  · -- dimension one: the class of `1` spans
541	    intro hdeg f hf
542	    -- `[1] ≠ 0`, and in a 1-dimensional space a nonzero vector spans
543	    have hspan : ∀ z : localStepTgt k P 1, ∃ c : k,
544	        z = c • Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.comap
545	          (orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)).subtype (orderGeSub k P 1)) ⟨1, hone⟩ := by
546	      intro z
547	      haveI := nontrivial_localStepTgt_one k P
548	      have hne : Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.comap
549	          (orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)).subtype (orderGeSub k P 1))
550	          (⟨1, hone⟩ : orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)) ≠ 0 := by
551	        intro h
552	        rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply,
553	          mem_orderGeSub] at h
554	        rcases h with h0 | h0
555	        · exact one_ne_zero h0
556	        · rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_one] at h0; norm_num at h0
557	      -- a nonzero vector in a space of rank 1 spans it
558	      have hfr : Module.finrank k (localStepTgt k P 1) = 1 := hdeg
559	      obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := (finrank_eq_one_iff_of_nonzero' _ hne).mp hfr z
560	      exact ⟨c, hc.symm⟩
561	    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hspan (Submodule.Quotient.mk
562	      (p := Submodule.comap (orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)).subtype (orderGeSub k P 1))

622	
623	Under `HasRationalResidues` at every prime divisor — the substrate's form of "the base
624	field is algebraically closed" — the two hypotheses that §4 and `SectionBounds.lean` §4
625	left open both become discharged simultaneously, because both were the same fact:
626	
627	* the uniform generation bound gets `r = 1`, so the threshold is `b + 1`;
628	* `deg_k = deg` (`degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one`), so the weighted statements
629	  become statements about the geometric degree — in particular the principal-degree-zero
630	  leaf.
631	
632	This is the precise pay-off of §5: one approximation hypothesis, two consequences.
633	-/

638	    [IsNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
639	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
640	
641	/-- **Rational residues everywhere give residue degree one everywhere.** -/
642	theorem residueDeg_eq_one_of_hasRationalResidues
643	    (hres : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, HasRationalResidues k P)
644	    [∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)]
645	    (P : X.PrimeDivisor) : residueDeg k P = 1 :=
646	  (residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues k P).mpr (hres P)
647	
648	/-- **Uniform global generation with threshold `b + 1`.**  With rational residues at
649	every point, the residue-degree bound of `exists_bound_forall_generatedAt` is `r = 1`, so
650	one threshold works for every point and the shift over the vanishing bound is a single
651	unit.
652	
653	This is the classical shape: above `deg D ≥ b + 1`, `𝒪(D)` is generated by global
654	sections everywhere.  It remains single-field. -/
655	theorem exists_bound_forall_generatedAt_of_hasRationalResidues
656	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
657	    (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D₀))
658	    (hpeel : ∀ D' : X.WeilDivisor,
659	      (∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P ≤
660	        (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) →
661	      Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D')

663	    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k ⊤ D)]
664	    [∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
665	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D →
666	      ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, GeneratedAt k D P :=
667	  exists_bound_forall_generatedAt k U₀ U₁ hledger D₀ hbase hpeel 1
668	    (fun P => le_of_eq (residueDeg_eq_one_of_hasRationalResidues k hres P))

670	/-- **The weighted degree is the geometric degree, under rational residues.**  Together

676	    [∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)]

678	  degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one k
679	    (fun P _ => residueDeg_eq_one_of_hasRationalResidues k hres P)

work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.

## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).

Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:

- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
  as **memory**.

Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

## Resuming after an interruption

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and
`## Why I stopped`). In `## Progress`, one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop.

## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)

There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
`subagents` skill):

- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

330	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
